# sysutils_service (Resource)

Manages the runtime state of an existing service: whether it starts at boot and whether it is running, and restarts it when any value in `restart_on_change` changes. Uses `systemctl` when systemd booted the host and `rc-service`/`rc-update` when OpenRC did, as on Alpine Linux. The service itself must already exist; install it with `sysutils_package` or define it with `sysutils_systemd_unit`. Destroying the resource leaves the service as it is. Requires root privileges.

`sysutils_service` complements [`sysutils_systemd_unit`](./systemd_unit.md), which manages unit files that you write yourself: use `sysutils_service` for services that a package installed, for services on OpenRC hosts, and to restart a service when its configuration files change.

On Terraform 1.14 and later, the [`sysutils_service` action](../actions/service.md) is an alternative to `restart_on_change`: invoked from the `action_trigger` of the resource that writes the configuration, it restarts or reloads the service right after the file is written, including when it is first created. `restart_on_change` works with every Terraform and OpenTofu version.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Install nginx, keep it enabled and running, and restart it whenever its
# configuration changes. Works with systemd and with OpenRC (Alpine).
resource "sysutils_package" "nginx" {
  name = "nginx"
}

resource "sysutils_file" "nginx_conf" {
  path    = "/etc/nginx/conf.d/app.conf"
  content = "server { listen 8080; root /srv/www; }\n"

  depends_on = [sysutils_package.nginx]
}

resource "sysutils_service" "nginx" {
  name    = "nginx"
  enabled = true
  state   = "running"

  restart_on_change = {
    config = sysutils_file.nginx_conf.content_sha256
  }

  depends_on = [sysutils_package.nginx]
}

# Keep a service that a package enabled from running at boot, and stop it.
resource "sysutils_service" "avahi" {
  name    = "avahi-daemon.service"
  enabled = false
  state   = "stopped"
}

# Only report whether a service is running; change nothing.
resource "sysutils_service" "sshd" {
  name = "ssh.service"
}

output "sshd_running" {
  value = sysutils_service.sshd.state == "running"
}
```

To manage a unit file and its runtime state separately, reference the unit's name so that the unit is created first. Leave `enabled` and `state` unset on the `sysutils_systemd_unit` in that case, so that the two resources don't both manage them:

```terraform
resource "sysutils_systemd_unit" "app" {
  name   = "app.service"
  source = "${path.module}/app.service"
}

resource "sysutils_service" "app" {
  name    = sysutils_systemd_unit.app.name
  enabled = true
  state   = "running"
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the service. With systemd, a unit name such as `"nginx.service"`, `"nginx"` (short for `nginx.service`), `"getty@tty2.service"` or `"backup.timer"`; aliases are resolved to the unit they name. A template unit such as `"getty@.service"` cannot be managed itself, only its instances. With OpenRC, the name of a script in `/etc/init.d`, such as `"nginx"`. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the service starts at boot: `systemctl enable`/`disable`, or with OpenRC `rc-update add`/`del` in `runlevel`. If unset, the enablement is not managed and the current value is reported. With systemd, only `enabled` counts as enabled; `static`, `indirect`, `enabled-runtime` and `masked` units are reported as not enabled, and only units with an `[Install]` section can be enabled.
- `restart_on_change` (Map of String) Arbitrary map of values whose change restarts the service, like the `triggers_replace` of `terraform_data`, but updating in place. Use it to restart the service when its configuration changes, for example with the `content_sha256` of a `sysutils_file`. The values are not passed to the service. Only a running service is restarted, and never while `state` is `"stopped"`; a service started by the same apply is not restarted again. Setting the map for the first time, including on create, does not restart the service; removing it does not either. With systemd, `systemctl daemon-reload` runs before the restart, so that changed unit files and drop-ins take effect.
- `runlevel` (String) OpenRC runlevel that `enabled` refers to. Defaults to `"default"`, the runlevel that `rc-update add` uses. A service is enabled when it is in this runlevel, whatever other runlevels it is in. Ignored with systemd.
- `state` (String) Whether the service should be `"running"` or `"stopped"`. If unset, the service is not started or stopped and the current value is reported. With systemd, a unit counts as running when `systemctl is-active` reports `active`, `reloading` or `refreshing`; with OpenRC, when `rc-service <name> status` reports `started`.
- `timeout` (String) Maximum time each `systemctl`, `rc-service` or `rc-update` invocation may take, as a Go duration such as `"30s"` or `"5m"`. Starting, stopping and restarting wait for the service, so this should exceed its own start and stop timeouts. Defaults to `"2m"`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Resource identifier (equal to `name`).
- `init_system` (String) Init system that manages the service: `"systemd"` or `"openrc"`. Detected on every plan: systemd if `/run/systemd/system` exists, which systemd creates when it is PID 1; otherwise OpenRC if `/run/openrc/softlevel` exists. If neither exists, planning fails.

## Init System Detection

The init system is detected on every plan and apply, and the result is shown in `init_system`:

| Init system | Detected when | Commands |
|-------------|---------------|----------|
| systemd | `/run/systemd/system` exists, which systemd creates when it runs as PID 1 (the check of `sd_booted()`) | `systemctl show`, `is-enabled`, `is-active`, `enable`, `disable`, `start`, `stop`, `restart` |
| OpenRC | `/run/openrc/softlevel` exists, which OpenRC creates when it boots the host (the check `rc-service` itself makes) | `rc-service --exists`, `rc-service <name> status`/`start`/`stop`/`restart`, `rc-update show`/`add`/`del` |

If neither exists, as in most containers, planning fails with a `No supported init system` error that names the markers it looked for and the process running as PID 1. The commands must be in the provider's `PATH`.

## Behavior

### Create and Update

1. The provider checks that the service exists: systemd must know the unit (its load state is not `not-found`), or OpenRC must have a script for it in `/etc/init.d`. If not, the apply fails with `Service not found`; nothing is recorded in state, and the next apply tries again.
2. If `enabled` is set and differs from the current value, the service is enabled or disabled.
3. If `state` is set and differs from the current value, the service is started or stopped.
4. On update, if `restart_on_change` changed and the service was running before this apply, it is restarted. A service that this apply started or stopped, or that is to be stopped, is not restarted.

With systemd, a restart runs `systemctl daemon-reload` first, so that a changed unit file or drop-in (such as `/etc/systemd/system/nginx.service.d/override.conf`) takes effect. systemd does not report a drop-in created since the last reload as needing one, so the reload is unconditional. Starting a unit reloads only if systemd reports `NeedDaemonReload=yes`.

Each change is checked by reading the status back. Enabling a systemd unit without an `[Install]` section, or starting a service that exits right away, fails the apply instead of leaving a permanent diff. If a restart fails, the previous `restart_on_change` stays in state, so the next apply restarts again.

With systemd, the name is first resolved to the unit's primary name with `systemctl show --property=Id`: `nginx` becomes `nginx.service`, and an alias such as `sshd.service` becomes the unit it points to (`ssh.service` on Debian and Ubuntu), because `systemctl enable` refuses aliases.

### Destroy

Destroying the resource only removes it from state. The service keeps running, or stays stopped, and stays enabled or disabled. To stop a service when the resource is removed, apply `state = "stopped"` first.

## Drift Detection

On refresh the provider reads the current enablement and state:

- systemd: `enabled` is `true` only when `systemctl is-enabled` reports `enabled`; `enabled-runtime`, `static`, `indirect`, `masked` and the like count as `false`. `state` is `"running"` when `systemctl is-active` reports `active`, `reloading` or `refreshing`, and `"stopped"` otherwise, including `failed` and `activating`.
- OpenRC: `enabled` is `true` when `rc-update show <runlevel>` lists the service. `state` is `"running"` when `rc-service <name> status` reports `started`, and `"stopped"` otherwise, including `crashed`.
- With `enabled` or `state` unset in the configuration, the current value is recorded in state but never changed, and never shows up as a diff. `state` is shown as `(known after apply)` when `restart_on_change` changes, and `enabled` when `runlevel` changes.
- If the service no longer exists, the resource is removed from state, and the next plan creates it again, which fails until the service is back.

## Timeouts

Every `systemctl`, `rc-service` and `rc-update` invocation is limited by `timeout` (2 minutes by default) and killed when it expires, which fails the apply. Starting, stopping and restarting wait for the service, so choose a `timeout` longer than the service's own start and stop timeouts.

## Import

An existing service can be imported by name:

```shell
# By service name, as for systemctl or rc-service. The service must exist.
terraform import sysutils_service.nginx nginx
```

After import, `enabled`, `state` and `init_system` reflect the service's current status, `runlevel` and `timeout` are set to their defaults and `restart_on_change` is unset.

## Caveats

- The resource requires root, and systemd or OpenRC as the host's init system. With systemd it manages the system instance only, not user units (`systemctl --user`).
- With OpenRC, `enabled` refers to one runlevel. A service in the `boot` runlevel counts as not enabled with the default `runlevel = "default"`; set `runlevel = "boot"` to manage it there.
- It refuses to plan when the provider's `root_dir` is set: services always run on the host.
- A `Type=oneshot` systemd service without `RemainAfterExit=yes` becomes inactive as soon as it has run, so `state = "running"` fails for it.
- Don't manage the same unit's `enabled` or `state` from both `sysutils_service` and `sysutils_systemd_unit`; the two would undo each other's changes.
